textos.acao.instalar.aviso: Installs and enables the role on this machine. May take minutes (apt) and changes its configuration.
textos.acao.iniciar.aviso: Starts the role's service, which is already installed here.
textos.acao.parar.aviso: Stops the service and removes it from boot (it will not come back on its own when the machine restarts). The configuration stays; what it was doing stops being done until it returns. On the Routing role this WIPES the firewall: the LAN loses internet and the machine is left exposed. A service that was already on the machine before GHop is only STOPPED, and stays enabled at boot.
textos.acao.desinstalar.aviso: Stops the service and undoes what the installer did, restoring the previous configuration. Does NOT delete collected data.

textos.texto.entidades_que_voce_ja:
Entities you have already looked at and decided on. Registered: it went into the inventory. Dismissed: you looked and decided not to add it — kept so it stops looking new.

textos.texto.cruzamento_de_quatro_leituras:
Four readings of each node, crossed: the ARP/NDP table (who spoke), DHCP (who holds an address of ours), Wi-Fi (who is on the radio) and the interfaces. There is no scanning — not one extra packet enters the observed network.
It is a TREE, not a graph: the node sees the internet above, its segments and who is on each one — a device talking to a device on the same LAN does not pass through it, so a line between two hosts would be an invention.
Unlike the other Inventory windows, this one talks to the nodes: it stores nothing and changes on every Refresh.

textos.cli.ajuda:
GHop panel, command-line shell.

A "node" is an observed machine. The panel is what knows the nodes: an agent
has no idea any other exists. A node's primary key is its NAME, never its
address -- registering the same name again only changes the address.

Usage:
  ./ghop-painel.py nos                            list the registered nodes
  ./ghop-painel.py nos adicionar <node> <address> register or update
  ./ghop-painel.py nos remover <node>
  ./ghop-painel.py resumo <node> [key=value ...]  read the node's counters
  ./ghop-painel.py listas                         show the allow list
  ./ghop-painel.py listas adicionar <kind> <type> <value> [note]
  ./ghop-painel.py listas remover <kind> <index>
  ./ghop-painel.py filtro <node>                  read the application filter
  ./ghop-painel.py vizinhos <node>                the node's raw ARP/NDP table
  ./ghop-painel.py conexoes <node>                map of who talked to whom
  ./ghop-painel.py topologia <node>               who is on its network, crossed

Reads only. Writing a filter rule is done in the window: it is a command that
cuts LAN traffic, and the confirmation saying what falls with it belongs there.

The verbs stay as they are in every language: they are what you type.

Examples:
  ./ghop-painel.py nos adicionar gateway 192.168.101.1
  ./ghop-painel.py nos adicionar gateway 192.168.101.1:7000
  ./ghop-painel.py resumo gateway
  ./ghop-painel.py resumo gateway limite=50 dia=02_09_2026
  ./ghop-painel.py --json resumo gateway

Options:
  --json          print the raw answer, for scripts
  --sem-testar    register without checking the handshake (machine powered off)
  --tudo          also show what the allow list covers

Environment variables:
  GHOP_PAINEL        panel name (default: the only one issued, if there is one)
  GHOP_CA_DIR        CA directory (default: ~/.ghop/ca)
  GHOP_PAINEL_SENHA  password of the panel key (otherwise it asks on the terminal)
  GHOP_IDIOMA        interface language: en (default), pt, tlh
